_strings.@@60dcbc50a58b: Indiana Earned Income Credit (EIC) — You must be eligible for and have actually claimed the federal Earned Income Credit on your federal return; if you did not claim the federal EIC you cannot claim the Indiana EIC. For 2023 and later Indiana follows all federal EIC requirements and allowances (the prior Indiana-specific modifications no longer apply). Schedule IN-EIC (including dependent information) must be completed and enclosed by all filers claiming the credit. Part-year residents get an apportioned credit.

_strings.@@77c3dc141764: Treaty conformity — IN conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from IN income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the IN return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Indiana's resident return (Form IT-40) starts from federal adjusted gross income: Line 1 instructs "Enter the adjusted gross income from your federal Form 1040/1040-SR, line 11." Income exempt from federal tax under a U.S. tax treaty is already excluded from federal AGI, so it flows through to Indiana untaxed. The only Indiana additions are Schedule 1: Add-Backs, which are all IRC-conformity / decoupling items (bonus depreciation, NOL deduction, out-of-state municipal obligation interest, Section 179, excess business losses (461(l)), excess federal interest (163(j)), federal repatriated dividends (965), employer student loan payments, conformity codes 120/147, etc.). The full Schedule 1 add-back list contains NO line for treaty-exempt or U.S.-tax-treaty income, and a full-text search of both the IT-40 and IT-40PNR 2023 booklets returns zero references to "treaty." Because IN starts from federal AGI and has no treaty add-back, federally treaty-exempt income is NOT re-taxed -> conforms. (Contrast with CA, which adds treaty income back on Schedule CA.)
_strings.@@83a047841ff8: Indiana DOR - 2023 IT-40 Full-Year Resident Individual Income Tax Booklet (Line 1 federal AGI start; Schedule 1 Add-Backs list - no treaty add-back; residency definitions; due date April 15, 2024; mailing addresses; check payee DOR; INTIME; filing requirement/exemption thresholds)
_strings.@@89fc8181e6f6: Indiana529 / CollegeChoice 529 Education Savings Plan Credit — Any Indiana taxpayer (single, married filing jointly, or married filing separately) who makes a contribution to an Indiana529 (formerly CollegeChoice 529) Savings Plan account during the tax year; the taxpayer need not be the account owner. Credit offsets only state adjusted gross income tax liability and cannot be used against county tax. Claimed on Schedule IN-529.
_strings.@@ab9e84168833: Lake County (Indiana) Residential Income Tax Credit — Available only to residents who paid property tax to Lake County, Indiana on their principal residence (owned or being bought under contract); whose Modified Indiana Adjusted Gross Income is less than $18,600; and who are NOT claiming the Homeowner's Residential Property Tax Deduction on Indiana Schedule 2, line 2. This is the closest Indiana equivalent to a property-tax credit but is limited to Lake County residents (not statewide).
_strings.@@b82a60d19f89: Unified Tax Credit for the Elderly — You and/or your spouse must have been age 65 or older by Dec. 31, 2023; if married and living together at any time during the year you must file a joint return; you must have been an Indiana resident for at least six months during 2023; and you must not have been in prison for 180 days or more in 2023. Disabled persons under age 65 do not qualify. The credit must be claimed within three years of the return's filing due date. Low-income filers not otherwise required to file may claim it on the simplified Form SC-40; others claim it on Form IT-40 line 5. File either SC-40 or IT-40, not both.
_strings.@@bd88c30bfb1c: Law change NOT modeled by the engine (status final_form_published): Indiana Earned Income Credit CONFORMED TO THE FEDERAL EIC for 2023 and later — "For the 2023 tax year, Indiana follows all requirements and allowances for the federal EIC." (the prior Indiana-specific modifications no longer apply). The credit remains 10% of the federal EIC, but eligibility now tracks the federal rules exactly, and Schedule IN-EIC (including dependent information) must be completed and enclosed by all filers claiming it; part-year residents receive an apportioned credit. Resolve via: Schedule IN-EIC and the 2023 IT-40 booklet Schedule 5 Line 6 instructions (10% of the federal EIC, with the Form IT-40 line 1 income ceiling of $63,398) — plus Income Tax Information Bulletin #92 at the citation URL. calc.state_tax computes only the 3.15% state line, so the credit is applied after it.

_strings.@@d54cfeaa9c24: Indiana DOR Income Tax Information Bulletin #92, 'Individual Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) Procedures' (March 2024), corroborated by 2023 IT-40 Booklet (Schedule 5, line 6)
_strings.@@d69bc4cca3ee: Adoption Credit — You are eligible to claim the Indiana adoption credit if you claimed an adoption credit on your federal return (federal Form 8839). A credit may also be allowed based on a federal adoption credit carryforward from the preceding five tax years (2018-2022).

state_tax.work_common_tail: 0. Tax line: IT-40 Line 8: "State adjusted gross income tax: multiply line 7 by 3.15% (.0315)" (Line 7 = Indiana adjusted gross income = Line 5 minus Line 6 exemptions; Line 1 starts from federal AGI). Verified exemption kinds shipped but NOT applied by this op (compute them on the form): additional_dependent_child ($1,500 — Schedule 3 Line 3: additional $1,500 per qualifying dependent CHILD (under 19, or a full-time student under 24). NOT applied by calc.state_tax — enter it on Schedule 3 Line 3.); adopted_child ($3,000 — Schedule 3 Line 6: additional $3,000 per adopted child. NOT applied by calc.state_tax.); age_65_low_income ($500 — Schedule 3 Line 5: additional $500 per 65-or-older box when IT-40 Line 1 (federal AGI) is under $40,000 (under $20,000 married filing separately). NOT applied by calc.state_tax.); age_65_or_blind ($1,000 — Schedule 3 Line 4: $1,000 per 65-or-older / blind checkbox. NOT applied by calc.state_tax.) This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: First-year $3,000 dependent-child amount (instead of $1,500) has NARROWER mechanics than first-year-claimed — per the 2023 IT-40 booklet it is allowed only in "the first taxable year in which the additional dependent exemption is allowable for that child" and is "not permitted if the child could have been claimed for the $1,500 exemption in any previous year, regardless of whether the child had been claimed." Eligibility gates on could-have-claimed, not first-actually-claimed — decide it on Schedule 3, not here. Indiana COUNTY income taxes (IT-40 Schedule CT-40, county rates) are NOT modeled — calc.state_tax computes the state 3.15% line only; most Indiana filers also owe a county add-on.
